text:
anya: Quick checkpoint — we need to finalize who owns what in the autoscale surface for Dedicated GPU pools. Can we agree on a split today?

mike: Agree. My slice: admission (should request be admitted to headroom/burst) + immediate fallbacks. Not metering.

tom: I was thinking admission can be split: operator handles cluster-level constraints, runtime handles tenant-level quota checks. Operator returns an admit token.

anya: That matches the intent in the RFC but we need to be explicit about race windows and token lifetime. Short-lived tokens avoid double-spend.

lorna: +1. Also add a simple API: /admit?tenant=&pool= returns {allowed, token, reason}. Keep payloads tiny for perf.

mike: Implementation question: who enforces token revocation when pool drains? Operator or runtime? I vote operator (has global view).

tom: Operator should emit revocation events. Runtime subscribes and stops scheduling when token revoked. Avoid synchronous RPCs during eviction.

anya: Good. Also need a safety fallback for operator unavailability: runtime should apply a conservative local policy (reduce headroom, allow smaller bursts) instead of full deny.

lorna: Concurrency: if two admission requests race for last GPU, the operator should serialize decisions and return deterministic responses (first-commit wins). We'll expose request_id in logs for tracing.

mike: Observability: expose these metrics -> admit_attempts, admit_denied_reason, tokens_issued, tokens_revoked, avg_admit_latency. Dashboards per-pool.

tom: Can we have a tiny pseudo policy that operator runs? e.g.:
```
if (pool.available_gpus > burst_threshold) allow
else if (tenant_balance >= credit_needed) allow && deduct_credit
else deny(reason=insufficient_credits)
```

anya: Nice. For the runtime API surface we should support: validate_token(token) (fast), prewarm_request(token, shape), and revocation hook. Keep validate_token O(1).

lorna: For backward-compat we can fallback to a "best-effort" admit when operator returns 5xx but mark tokens with short TTL and instrument counts.

mike: Security note: tokens must be scoped (tenant+pool) and signed by operator KMS. No plain UUIDs.

orch-bot: Deploy plan reminder — staged rollout: 10% operator instances -> monitor admit_denied_rate -> 50% -> full. Alert on >2x baseline deny rate. :robot_face:

anya: Action items: mike to sketch operator API + token format, tom to prototype revocation stream, lorna to add metrics and dashboard layout. I'll pull together a concise follow-up RFC addendum with the decision boundaries.

mike: I'll post API proto by EOD. :thumbsup:

tom: Will mock a revocation simulator tomorrow.

lorna: I'll add dashboards and alert queries to the ops board.

anya: Thanks — closing this checkpoint. If anyone needs a deeper call ping me.
